context: Grading an original briefing-scene sketch about a corporate executive defending a post-scandal rebrand, judged for scene framing, dry character-driven tone, escalation, and a landed ending.

checklist.name: scene_framed_as_briefing
checklist.description: The output is written as a scene (briefing address plus at least one questioner/interjection), not prose narration or a description of the rebrand.

checklist.name: dry_character_driven_tone
checklist.description: Humour comes from the executive's evasive, formal self-justification rather than slapstick or random unconnected jokes.

checklist.name: escalation_and_euphemism
checklist.description: The scene builds across more than one beat and includes at least one clear euphemistic substitution for the scandal or its cover story.

checklist.name: landed_ending
checklist.description: The sketch closes on a definite beat: revealing admission, self-contradiction, or calmly stated absurdity.

checklist.name: sincerity_maintained
checklist.description: The executive never explicitly acknowledges, in their own voice, that the rebrand is a cover-up.
